1.	On April 25, 1719, a London publisher released a book that opens with the words: "I was born in the year 1632, in the city of York." The novel's full original title was almost comically long at 57 words in the tradition of the time. It has since been abbreviated to the name of its hero, X. The book is widely considered one of the first true English novels. The author Y based the story partly on the documented case of Scotsman Alexander Selkirk who spent four years and four months alone on a Pacific island before being rescued in 1709. In the novel, X spends 28 years on his island before being rescued. He teaches himself to make pottery, grow grain, bake bread, and domesticate goats. The book was so influential that German scholars coined the word ________ade for the entire genre of castaway and survival fiction it spawned — a lineage that runs through Jules Verne, The Swiss Family ________, Lord of the Flies, and the film Cast Away. Y was a merchant and trader, spent time in debtor's prison, and wrote extensively on trade with Asia and Africa. Name X (10 points) and Y (10 points). The two blanks are the same and they are the first name of X.

2.	In the spring of 1507, a small group of scholars gathered under the leadership of German scholar Martin Waldseemüller in the quiet Lorraine town of Saint-Dié to work on a new comprehensive visual representation of recent discoveries. On April 25, 1507, they published this pamphlet titled _Cosmographiae Introductio_. It is the first time the word X was used in its current geographical meaning. It is also the first European document to depict Y as a distinct body, albeit under the name “_______ Orientalis Indicus” instead of Y. Europeans would only reach Y for the first time five years later in 1512 from Y’s west through expeditions ordered by Afonso de Albuquerque. They would reach it from Y’s east in 1513 when Vasco Núñez de Balboa crossed an isthmus. Z reached Y in 1520 and gave it its current name because he found it much quieter compared to the notorious passage that he had just crossed to reach it.
